parsedVerdict.reasoning:
This module fails the rule because its two services handle data access in different ways. Both services deal with appointments, so they belong to one concern. But they don't share an abstraction. SchedulingService goes through the persistence DAOs (PatientDao, AppointmentDao). It turns rows into domain entities (Patient, Practitioner, Appointment) and reports failures with the domain error SchedulingError. VisitNotesService skips that layer. It calls PrismaService.visitNote.create/findMany directly, defines its own plain VisitNote interface instead of a domain entity, and builds note IDs and timestamps inline. That is a bypass of the module's own data-access approach.

Both files also repeat their row-to-object mapping. SchedulingService rebuilds an Appointment from a row in two places: inside book() (the sameDay .map) and in cancel(). VisitNotesService writes the row-to-VisitNote mapping twice: in write() and in notesFor(). Each mapping should live in one place.

violations.message: It skips the module's DAO-and-entity approach. It calls PrismaService.visitNote.create/findMany directly and returns a plain VisitNote interface. SchedulingService instead uses PatientDao/AppointmentDao and domain entities. It also writes the row-to-VisitNote mapping twice, in write() and in notesFor().
The row-to-Appointment mapping (new Appointment(a.id, ..., a.status as AppointmentStatus)) is written twice, in book() and cancel(), when it should live in one place.
